races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sole Ruler
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator returning over 6f after 43 days off, having run 4th and 7th in both career starts on Good ground; Paul Mulrennan will need a pace collapse to get competitive from the rear in a small field with a single front-runner controlling tempo.

runners_data.name: Reflect On Glory
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly with just one career run (3rd, 6f, Good), trained by K.R. Burke whose yard is firing at 10/42 over 14 days; style is unresolved which adds tactical uncertainty, but her form basis is thin and she may lack the seasoning for a sharp novice skirmish.

runners_data.name: The Mean Fiddler
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner stepping up to 6f from 5f after a 2nd on debut, wearing a tongue-tie; Jason Hart will use the small field to control tempo entirely, and uncontested lead on a flat, fast-draining Good surface is the ideal setup for this profile.

runners_data.name: War Gaming
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with 2-3 in back-to-back starts, both on Good going over 5f and 6f; fitted with a hood for the first time, and Cieren Fallon is likely to track The Mean Fiddler closely — the question is whether War Gaming can sustain that proximity and pounce late rather than simply accompany the leader.

races.paceDynamic: The Mean Fiddler is the lone confirmed front-runner in this four-horse field and, with no rival willing or able to seriously contest the lead, will dictate from the gates at a tempo entirely of Jason Hart's choosing on Good ground at Ripon. War Gaming is the only horse likely to press forward in proximity, but as a prominent type rather than a challenger for the lead, The Mean Fiddler faces no genuine pressure and can set a controlled, honest gallop over the six furlongs. Sole Ruler will settle in rear under Paul Mulrennan, while Reflect On Glory's unresolved style leaves some ambiguity about where Clifford Lee will position her, though she is unlikely to contest the pace. This uncontested lead on a flat course with Good ground and a small field is a textbook scenario that favours the horse who controls the tempo — the front-running profile holds a decisive positional advantage, and hold-up horses face the task of generating momentum from the back of a slowly-strung-out field with no pace to hide behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fiddler Leads, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If The Mean Fiddler sets a comfortable uncontested gallop and War Gaming cannot sustain close enough pressure to force a true test of pace.
scenarios.body: The Mean Fiddler, granted a stress-free lead, controls every yard and simply needs to find a gear in the final furlong; at 6f on Good ground with only four rivals, the lack of pace pressure typically rewards the leader who can quicken off their own tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Mean Fiddler sets a faster pace than expected and tires in the final furlong, leaving the race open for hold-up horses to swoop.
scenarios.body: Sole Ruler, dropping back to 6f having run over this trip before, would be the primary beneficiary if the field strings out and there is a genuine late collapse from the leader; Reflect On Glory, with just one career run but a placed effort over this exact course and trip, could also benefit from a generous finishing window.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: War Gaming Stays Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If War Gaming, fresh off back-to-back placed efforts and fitted with a hood, travels powerfully throughout and pegs back The Mean Fiddler close home.
scenarios.body: War Gaming's consistent form figures of 2-3 and recent 6f placed effort suggest she handles this trip well and, if The Mean Fiddler's lead is modest enough, a prominent pressing run could yield a late surge; Cieren Fallon's cold tactical awareness makes this a plausible secondhand winner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Reflect On Glory Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Reflect On Glory, lightly raced with a single career run, shows unexposed ability to track and quicken past more experienced rivals.
scenarios.body: With only one run to her name, the K.R. Burke yard's 10/42 14-day record suggests active form, and there is legitimate upside if she has improved markedly since her debut third; however, the lack of race experience and style uncertainty makes this scenario the least probable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether War Gaming's hood triggers a more forward, aggressive move from the gates — if she contests the lead rather than tracking, it would be the one factor capable of disrupting The Mean Fiddler's uncontested pace.

Sole Ruler is 43 days since her last run and has yet to win or place in two starts — if she is not sharper for the layoff, her hold-up style in a small field leaves her with almost no tactical recourse.

Reflect On Glory's unresolved running style means Clifford Lee's positioning decision in the first two furlongs is worth monitoring; if she is ridden prominently she becomes a far more interesting contender, if she drops in she faces the same problem as Sole Ruler.

The Mean Fiddler steps up 1f in trip to 6f — Hart will want to ensure the gallop is honest enough to test the closers but not so fast that it leaves the filly vulnerable in the final furlong having set her own pace from the off.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Queen Sana
runners_data.note: Multiple placed efforts (four seconds) on good ground over 5-6f; Daniel Tudhope in the saddle is a strong booking and trainer Sangster is firing at 7/16 over 14 days — her genuine front-running instinct means she will press for position even if the map places her in the midfield bracket in this shape.

runners_data.name: Rohini
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's filly has recorded five consecutive finishes of 7th or 8th, all on softer or standard tracks, and her single run on good going produced the same outcome; a true hold-up runner who will struggle to find competitive late momentum in what is likely to be a steadily-run 6f.

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a confirmed tendency to fade in the finish and a 49-day absence; her record on good ground reads 12 starts without a win or place, and she has finished 9th-11th in her last five starts over this trip — headgear (h) noted but hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: All Good
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's filly returns after a 293-day break and has only two starts to her name, both on standard Southwell; the absence length is the overriding concern regardless of potential, and natural hold-up style means she needs the race to come to her on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Royale Union
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke operates at a solid 10/42 over 14 days and Clifford Lee is a competent booking; ran only 5 days ago and has raced twice over 7f, so the drop to 6f is an unknown — prominent style suits the expected race shape but trip suitability is unproven.

runners_data.name: Secret Harvest
runners_data.note: Conrad Allen's filly is the lone confirmed front-runner with a placed effort over this exact course and trip combination on good going; Cieren Fallon takes over from last time and she can simply coast to an uncontested lead — her style-fit flag reflects the field context rather than any inherent weakness in her racing profile.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Harvest is the confirmed sole pace-setter and will dictate from the front over this 6f on good Ripon turf, with no genuine rival to press or challenge her early sectionals. Queen Sana and Royale Union are both prominent types who will look to sit close behind, but with Secret Harvest uncontested, she can control tempo and dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop that plays directly to her strengths. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can all naturally secure their preferred position — Queen Sana is the most likely to settle into a close-up tracking role behind Secret Harvest, while Royale Union may find herself marginally further back than ideal. This race shape firmly favours the front-running and close-tracking profile: an uncontested, self-directed lead over 6f on good ground with no pace pressure is a scenario where the horse in front — and those pressing just behind — hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Harvest breaks cleanly and sets a controlled, sustainable pace unchallenged throughout.
scenarios.body: Secret Harvest dictates every yard from flag to finish, controls the tempo, and quickens away from the field in the final furlong without having faced a single challenger for the lead; this shape is ideal for a front-runner with a placed effort at this course and trip on good ground. Horses tracking close, particularly Queen Sana and Royale Union, are best placed to capitalise if the leader tires late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overwhelm Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Queen Sana and Royale Union both press Secret Harvest hard enough early to soften her, allowing one to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more pressured than expected as prominent runners compete for position, resulting in a stronger tempo that flattens the leader and leaves a close-tracking type to finish best of all. Queen Sana, with multiple placed efforts on good ground at 5-6f, is ideally positioned to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses after an over-fast early gallop, gifting a late run to closers.
scenarios.body: All Good or Aurora's Doublesix would need the pace to have been truly suicidal for this scenario to unfold, and Aurora's Doublesix has shown a worrying tendency to fade rather than finish — making this shape fragile. All Good's long absence (293 days) adds further doubt about whether she can execute a clean late run on return.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Upset, Chaotic Race
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners underperform their market positions and an unconsidered runner delivers a career-best effort in a muddled tempo.
scenarios.body: Rohini has shown no meaningful form on good going across five attempts and is racing out of her natural hold-up role here, so this scenario is highly dependent on an improbable sequence of events. Aurora's Doublesix's poor course record (consistent 9th-11th on good ground) limits confidence in any scenario that relies on this profile.

watchPoints.text: Secret Harvest's uncontested lead is the race-defining factor — if she breaks cleanly and crosses to the rail, she controls the tempo entirely and the race could be over as a contest well before the final furlong.

Queen Sana and Royale Union will both attempt to press into a prominent position early, creating a brief but important tactical scuffle in the first furlong that could affect settling — watch which one yields and drops back, as that runner's chance is significantly diminished.

All Good's 293-day absence for Julie Camacho is a significant red flag; horses returning after this length of time without a prep run often need the outing and can be best ignored in betting terms regardless of their market position.

Aurora's Doublesix is fitted with headgear and represents a trainer who has had a recent runner (1/3 over 14 days), but her course-and-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 12 attempts on good ground makes meaningful improvement a tall order.

Rohini's overseas form (all on Southwell's standard Tapeta surface) translates poorly to good Ripon turf — her single good-going run produced a 7th and her hold-up style is further compromised by likely being out-manoeuvred for rear position in this field.

races.name: Weatherbys Bloodstock Pro Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Creative Queen
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with hood (headgear), trained by William Haggas and ridden by Cieren Fallon — a strong jockey-trainer combination — but recent form has regressed from a win to finishes of 6th and 7th, and she faces a direct pace rival in Zoustar Dreams who may simply outgun her from the off.
runners_data.comment: Creative Queen won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving her strong claims off a mark of 72; the risk is that she has finished seventh in each of her last two starts.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old has solid 5f good-ground experience (9 runs, 2 wins, 2 places) and sits prominently, giving her a clean run through the race; she is proven at this exact trip and going combination more than any other runner, which gives her a live each-way claim if the front-runners wear each other down.
runners_data.comment: Marajito won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a genuine threat from stall one carrying 132 lb — though a run of three consecutive reverses since that victory, combined with a trainer striking at just 3%, is the concern.

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's filly has won her last two starts over 5f on good ground and holds the most recent course win in the field; her hold-up style is perfectly suited to a contested pace scenario, and James Sullivan's positive booking for the stable adds confidence that she is fit and primed.
runners_data.comment: Angel Numbers is the one to beat here, landing last time out and returning quickly after just 18 days with experience of today's trip and going in her favour; she carries 135 lb from stall four, but her rating of 81 puts her top of this field.

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Three wins from her last four, including two successive 5f victories on good ground, make her the form horse of the race; she is a bold-going front-runner who has shown she can win even when pressed, and if Jack Callan (claim) manages the pace battle with Creative Queen astutely, she has every chance of lasting home.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of five on our figures, Zoustar Dreams is hard to fancy despite three wins in her last six starts — though a fourth two starts back disrupts recent momentum. She has distance and going experience and is fresh enough at 16 days since her last outing.

runners_data.name: North West Gal
runners_data.note: 67 days off is the key caveat for John and Sean Quinn's filly — her best recent efforts came on standard going at Chester, and while she has won over 5f before, three runs on good ground show no wins; she maps prominently but fitness from the layoff must be taken on trust.
runners_data.comment: North West Gal brings a win and two further placings in her last five starts, has experience of today's trip and going, and a rating of 77 suggests she holds strong claims from stall three; the chief concern is that she returns after 67 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Creative Queen and Zoustar Dreams are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this sharp 5f at Ripon, with neither likely to concede willingly — Creative Queen carries hood headgear suggesting she needs to be organised quickly, while Zoustar Dreams arrives on a three-from-four winning streak and her connections will want her in her comfort zone up front. The resulting duel will set an honest, pressure-laden gallop that is unlikely to be artificially slow, meaning the pace will be genuine from flag to finish on good ground. North West Gal and Marajito sit prominently behind the two leaders, so the first three positions are crowded, leaving Angel Numbers as the sole hold-up operator arriving late from the back. This race shape — a truly-run sprint with two front-runners burning each other off — classically favours the closer or late-arriving prominent horse who can exploit a contested pace, making Angel Numbers' hold-up profile the standout tactical fit, with Marajito potentially capitalising if either leader ties up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Aids Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Creative Queen and Zoustar Dreams lock horns from the gate and sustain a genuinely pressured gallop throughout the 5f.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up through the first two furlongs, leaving them vulnerable in the final 100 yards as their effort tells; the hold-up runner swoops late down the centre or stands' side rail to mop up. Angel Numbers' recent course-winning form over 5f on good ground and her proven ability to finish powerfully from off the pace make her the primary beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two lead duellists gains a decisive advantage early and the other capitulates, allowing a solo breakaway.
scenarios.body: Zoustar Dreams, whose last four runs show three wins including back-to-back 5f victories on good ground, is most capable of asserting and setting a controlled pace once the rival falters; Creative Queen, in less convincing recent form, is the likelier to drop away if outgunned. A controlled solo lead at an honest but not suicidal gallop then becomes difficult to peg back, particularly over the minimum trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel between the front-runners is brief or one fades quickly, leaving a race-reading prominent horse to swoop at the right moment.
scenarios.body: Marajito and North West Gal both sit handy and are experienced at 5f on good going; Marajito's two wins in 15 good-ground starts at this trip suggest she can capitalise on a mid-race positional opportunity if the leaders overdo it without fully exhausting themselves. North West Gal's return from 67 days off adds uncertainty but her course experience is a minor plus.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Early Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are cautious breaking or tactical riding conspires to produce a slow early pace, turning the race into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: An unusually tardy start or traffic interference could see the field bunch, negating Angel Numbers' hold-up advantage and bringing the whole field into play in a scrambling finish; this scenario is unlikely given two genuine front-runners confirmed in the race, but a false start or stumble could create it. Zoustar Dreams and North West Gal, both capable of quickening sharply from a pack, would benefit most in a sprint-for-home scenario.

watchPoints.text: Creative Queen and Zoustar Dreams are both confirmed front-runners — watch for an early pace duel that could fatally compromise both their finishing efforts if neither concedes ground before the halfway point.

Angel Numbers is the sole hold-up horse in a 5-runner field and will be last into the straight; if there is any traffic at the two-furlong pole she has nowhere to go, making her run dependent on a clean outside passage.

North West Gal returns from 67 days absent and has not won on genuine good ground in her last six starts — if she fails to stride out freely early, her prominent pitch may become a liability rather than an asset.

Marajito's jockey Oisin McSweeney rides for a yard (Tim Easterby) whose 14-day strike rate of 3/87 is modest, but Marajito's own record of 2 wins and 2 places from 9 runs on good going at 5f makes her statistically the most course-going-trip-consistent runner in the field.

Zoustar Dreams carries the in-form flag with three wins in four but drops back to 5f having won her last two over 5f — watch whether Jack Callan settles her or goes toe-to-toe immediately with Creative Queen, as the former approach dramatically improves her chance of lasting home.

races.name: Wilmot-smith Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer with a course win over this C&D on Good ground and a second recent placing; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a meaningful weight concession and Nigel Tinkler's stable is running at 3/30 over 14 days — straightforward profile for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Lord Roxby brings fair recent form — second last time out and a winner four starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, but a fifth and fourth in between hint at inconsistency, and 131 lb is no gimme at this level.

runners_data.name: Saint Lawrence
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up operator for Kevin Ryan who has placed twice on Good going in this company; blinkers noted and 17 days since last run is fine, but his best recent form has come on Good rather than Soft, so conditions suit — dependent on a strong pace to close into.
runners_data.comment: Saint Lawrence was second three starts back and arrives fresh on 17 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going and a speed rating of 94 that marks him out as a genuine threat from stall 4; the concern is he's winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on OR=94 and a genuine front runner who should lead uncontested, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) flags that he may be operating outside his sharpest role; Daniel Tudhope is an excellent jockey for this type and the visor has been retained from his recent win.
runners_data.comment: Dark Cloud Rising arrives on a strong fitness pitch — a winner two starts back and placed last time out, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the main risk is whether he can reproduce that form under a stiff 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Michael Dods who has twice finished second over this C&D on Good ground in recent form; 9 days since last run is brisk but the yard is firing (5/30 in 14 days) and the hood kept on suggests a horse travelling well mentally.
runners_data.comment: Commanche Falls has shown consistent placing ability, finishing second in two of his last five starts, and returns here on a quick nine-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going. Carrying 137 lb from stall one, our rating of 105 marks him the one to beat, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's hold-up specialist is a true rear-of-field type pushed into a mapped midfield slot because the field is overloaded with closers; recent form is very moderate (five runs without a win) and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — not his ideal scenario even if the pace does collapse.
runners_data.comment: Rousing Encore drops into a winnable spot on his rating of 88 and has run over today's trip and going, while third two starts back shows the spark is still there; the risk is a run of unplaced efforts either side of that makes consistency the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Tim Easterby who is yet to win in nine career starts; Sean Kirrane takes over and the 9-day turnaround is fine, but finishing positions of 10-12-9-10 over similar trips signal limited scope to threaten from the rear on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Boston Dan faces a stiff ask here; his trainer is in poor form at 3% over the past fortnight, and while he has run over today's trip and going before and returns quickly on nine days' rest, little in the recent record encourages.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's seven-year-old is flagged for finishing fades and is a true hold-up runner shown in midfield only because hold-up types outnumber available rear positions; OR=77 is the lowest in the field and Midgley has 0 wins from 21 runners in 14 days — significant negatives stacked against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts with three consecutive unplaced runs, Grant Wood faces a stiff ask ranked last on our figures; the trainer's current 0/21 run compounds concerns, though he has run over today's trip and going before and is fit enough at ten days.

races.paceDynamic: Dark Cloud Rising is the confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press from the outside, should be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground at Ripon's straight 6f. Lord Roxby and Commanche Falls will track closely in prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early order with the trio covering the first two furlongs in unison. The hold-up horses — Saint Lawrence, Boston Dan, Rousing Encore, and Grant Wood — will be ridden into the back half of the field, needing a late surge on a track that historically rewards those who travel well in midfield rather than true closers from the rear. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead with a compact chasing pack — strongly favours prominent racers who can time their challenge off a sustainable pace, giving Lord Roxby and Commanche Falls the clearest tactical advantage. The field contains more hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear, with Rousing Encore and Grant Wood redistributed to mapped midfield positions, though their true instinct is to close late — meaning neither will naturally secure the ground that profile requires.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Cloud Rising bowls along uncontested and the pace stays honest but not blistering, allowing the chasers to strike entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Dark Cloud Rising dictates throughout on a flat, undemanding track and the prominent pair Lord Roxby and Commanche Falls track in his slipstream before challenging off the final bend. This shape rewards horses who race handily with enough stamina to sustain their effort over the final two furlongs, and both Lord Roxby and Commanche Falls have the form and style to do exactly that.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Cloud Rising is never seriously challenged and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in the final furlong on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Dark Cloud Rising, running prominent with a STYLE_FIT tag suggesting it may be racing out of true role but still capable at the top of the weights, finds the uncontested lead enough to repel rivals who cannot quicken from further back. The flat Ripon straight removes course-related excuses for closers and the Good ground offers no extra grip for late finishers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a genuine late closer threads through a tiring pack.
scenarios.body: Saint Lawrence, who has placed at this level on Good ground and uses hold-up tactics naturally, is best placed among the true closers to benefit if the front end ties up. This scenario requires the prominent horses to overcook the pace earlier than expected, which is unlikely given Dark Cloud Rising's confirmed ability to rate the gallop, but Saint Lawrence's course-appropriate form keeps it live.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Cloud Rising is crowded early or the pace fragments into multiple surges, leaving no single horse with a clean run.
scenarios.body: A messy race with no clear shape would theoretically bring the redistributed mid-pack types Rousing Encore and Grant Wood into play, though both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and have limited recent winning form. Grant Wood's finishing fade flag and Rousing Encore's inconsistent recent figures make this the least productive scenario for punters to pursue.

watchPoints.text: Lord Roxby is 14 days fresh, has a C&D win on Good ground, and gets a 3lb claim from Alex Jary — watch for him to press Dark Cloud Rising from early and challenge hardest inside the final furlong.

Dark Cloud Rising carries top weight of 140lbs and the STYLE_FIT tag suggests he is not in his sharpest role; if he over-races or fades after two furlongs of unchallenged lead, the race opens up for Commanche Falls behind him.

Commanche Falls has gone 9 days between runs and the hood is retained — watch his early behaviour in the stalls and the first furlong, as any sluggish break from a prominent draw would seriously compromise his chance in this race shape.

Saint Lawrence is the only hold-up horse with a recent placed run on Good going at this distance; if the pace is genuinely strong through the middle section, watch where he sits at the two-furlong pole — a position inside the final three would be a positive sign.

Grant Wood's finishing-fade flag is significant on a flat straight track where there is nowhere to hide; watch whether Jason Hart rides him more aggressively than his natural style suggests, which would confirm connections are abandoning the hold-up approach entirely.

races.name: North Yorkshire Ice Cream Championship 2026 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Progressive form string (464321) and a recent win over 10f on Good ground make this Ryan Kavanagh's (3lb claimer) most relevant ammunition; a prominent racer who should sit second and is the most likely beneficiary if Poet's Dawn weakens late, though the 16-day gap looks ideal for a fit, in-form four-year-old.
runners_data.comment: Everyoneknowsadave arrives in fine nick — a winner last time out, and a second two starts back — with experience of today's trip and going, and 16 days between runs suggesting he's fresh and ready. Stall 4 with 134 lb, he makes a strong case as our pick.

runners_data.name: Mao Shang Wong
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up specialist has a mixed record at similar level (4W/15 on Good), and a 29-day break plus form figure of 7 last time out raise questions about peak readiness; Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim helps, but this horse needs a stronger gallop than a solo leader is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Mao Shang Wong brings distance-and-going experience and a peak rating of 80 to back his claims, and that second two starts back underlines his quality on a good day; the risk is his seventh last time out, which he must put firmly behind him.

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: A 284-day absence is the dominant concern here — Tina Jackson sends him out fresh with a 1-from-5 trainer strike rate, and while Clifford Lee has the experience to place him prominently, the lack of a recent run over this course and a soft-ground bias in his history makes Good ground this trip a moderate but manageable query.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts — second three starts back, second four starts back, and second last time out in his last five — mark His Finest Hour as a genuine danger, and he has run over today's trip; the concern is 284 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners a lightly-raced four-year-old whose best form has come on Good ground (1W4P from nine runs) and who won over 8f just 8 days ago; the quick turnaround and hold-up style leaves him dependent on a pace scenario that this field may not generate, but Tristan Davidson's 2/10 fortnight form is a quiet positive.
runners_data.comment: Polygram arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, giving her a sharp upward curve in form that makes her a genuine threat here; the main risk is that she rates only fourth of the five on our figures.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran whose record of 4W/11 on Good and 11/15 sim-going runs tells a clear tale of durability; the headgear flag suggests connections are sharpening him for maximum effect, and with no rival likely to press him for the lead, Kirrane can dictate every yard of this 1m2f — the decisive tactical asset in this field.
runners_data.comment: Poet's Dawn has winning form in his recent starts — a winner two starts back and again last time out — but our figures rank him last of five here, and his trainer is in a dire spell at 3% over the past fortnight. The 130 lb burden won't help.

races.paceDynamic: Poet's Dawn is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 1m2f handicap at Ripon and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, will be able to control the tempo from the outset at a pace entirely of Sean Kirrane's choosing. Everyoneknowsadave and His Finest Hour are both prominent-style runners who will likely track Poet's Dawn in second and third, meaning the race will take on an orderly, single-file shape rather than a contested, strung-out affair. Mao Shang Wong and Polygram, both hold-up types, will be further back and will need a strong enough gallop to be set alight in the closing stages — but with only one pacesetter who has every incentive to nurse the gallop, that end-to-end tempo may never fully develop. This race shape distinctly favours hold-up horses only if the pace is genuinely strong; more likely it rewards a prominent racer who travels smoothly just behind a solo, unchallenged leader and produces the decisive effort at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poet's Dawn Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn is allowed to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop throughout the 1m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Kirrane pings Poet's Dawn out and settles into a measured rhythm, with Everyoneknowsadave and His Finest Hour unable or unwilling to apply pressure from behind; an 11-year-old veteran with four wins from 11 on Good ground and a headgear flag suggesting sharpening intentions, Poet's Dawn holds on as the field fails to generate the pace to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overwhelm Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave and His Finest Hour track closely and collectively swamp Poet's Dawn from the two-furlong marker.
scenarios.body: The prominent duo use their Good-ground course form and fresher handicap marks to overhaul the front-runner late, with the race turning into a battle between them in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn sets a genuinely strong gallop that strings the field out and leaves closers with a clear run through.
scenarios.body: Polygram, with nine Good-ground runs and an eye-catching recent win, or Mao Shang Wong, who recorded a Good-ground win from off the pace, would be the beneficiary as the field comes back to them in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested pace is so slow that the race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole with all five runners in contention.
scenarios.body: A muddling crawl benefits whoever has the sharpest turn of foot over 1m2f on Good turf, likely favouring the most in-form and freshest handicapper in the group.

watchPoints.text: Poet's Dawn's unchallenged lead is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if Kirrane gets a soft lead from the off, every other runner's task immediately becomes harder.

Everyoneknowsadave is the principal threat to the leader: watch whether Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claimer) elects to press Poet's Dawn early or sits patient, as that decision alone could shape whether the race develops into a true test.

His Finest Hour's 284-day absence is a significant fitness unknown — if Clifford Lee asks him to race prominently, watch how he responds under pressure in the final quarter-mile, as a well-beaten run from him would likely collapse any pace contest behind the leader.

Mao Shang Wong's win record shows he can produce from off the pace on Good ground, but his form figure of 7 last time needs explaining — if he travels smoothly in the rear without cover issues, he is the most dangerous outsider.

Polygram's quick 8-day turnaround merits monitoring in the paddock: if he looks sharp and well in himself, his Good-ground placed form at longer trips could make him a factor, but a hold-up horse in a small field with one pacesetter is tactically exposed.

races.name: Queen Ethelburga's Collegiate Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dacres Cross
runners_data.note: Best form is over 6-7f and this step up to a mile on Good looks stretching; hold-up style is her natural mode but the crowded rear of this field means she may be shuffled wider than ideal, limiting her finishing kick for Kevin Ryan.
runners_data.comment: Dacres Cross has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 75 by us against an official mark of 65, he merits respect as the top-rated runner; yet to score in his last five starts, he must convert that latent promise from stall six carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Vega's Virtue
runners_data.note: Dual winner over this trip and the mile on Good ground is a clear plus; races from hold-up and Tim Easterby's runners are in decent form (T14: 3/87), with the question being whether Fentiman can get her into a clean position given the congestion at the back of the field.
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning form last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, but a well-beaten eighth two starts back tempers enthusiasm, and her trainer is in poor nick at 3% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner carries a string of disappointing efforts including six straight finishes outside the frame; a genuine hold-up horse who will struggle to operate cleanly in midfield where the race map has placed him, and the sim-going figures (0W0P) offer little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Sailor's Return has experience over today's trip and conditions, and back-to-back fourths four and five starts back hint at ability worth respecting under a feather-light 133 lb from stall 3; the risk is she has been winless in recent starts, with an unplaced effort last time clouding her claims.

runners_data.name: Scheffler
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls sends him here after a modest recent sequence and the form note of fading in the finish is a real concern over a flat mile; naturally races from the rear but has been repositioned to midfield in this map — a horse whose best efforts have come over shorter when handy.

runners_data.name: Tago Mago
runners_data.note: Limited form base of just three runs with the best being a third at Catterick on Standard; true hold-up style will see Oisin Orr working through traffic, and with sim-going figures of just 1/3, the evidence for handling Good turf at this level is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Tago Mago has struggled of late — seventh last time out and eighth two starts back — though a third three starts back offers a sliver of encouragement, and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Amber Hamur
runners_data.note: The key pace angle in this race — a confirmed front-runner who won over 8f on Good and placed second over the same course and trip last time; Connor Beasley should get her loose and uncontested, making her the axis around which all tactical decisions are made.
runners_data.comment: Amber Hamur won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her some grounding, but a second two starts back is framed by three finishes outside the placings before that, and 130 lb from stall 8 is no gimme.

runners_data.name: Hey Havana
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with five top-five finishes in last five starts including two seconds over 7-8f on Good; Clifford Lee should slot her into the prominent position just off Amber Hamur's flank and her Ripon Good-ground form (sim-going 7/9) is a natural fit for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Hey Havana has finished in the first three three times in his last five starts and brings strong fitness — 28 days since his last run — along with experience of today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall one and carrying 128 lb, the main risk is he's yet to convert that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Itszaboy
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field on OR 52 and has not threatened the frame in any of his last six runs; Alex Jary claims 3lb but the horse's true hold-up style means he will be at the back of a crowded field, and the consistent stream of mid-division finishes gives little reason to expect a turnaround.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of mid-to-tail finishes, Itszaboy is hard to fancy from stall 4 carrying 122 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and our rating edges slightly above his official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Amber Hamur is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push her from the outside, she should stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the gates and control tempo at a sustainable gallop around Ripon's flat mile. Hey Havana will press forward into prominent position just behind her, but with only one horse truly setting the fractions, the early pace is unlikely to be pressured and the race will be run at a measured, even rhythm. That shape — a steady gallop with little acceleration until the two-furlong marker — classically rewards horses who travel prominently in the slipstream rather than those forced to produce a long-range finish from the back. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than can legitimately settle at the rear: Sailor's Return, Scheffler, Tago Mago and Itszaboy are all genuine hold-up types remapped to midfield, meaning several of them will be competing for the same ground and unable to race in their natural role. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the uncontested pace, produce a short sharp finish, and avoid the traffic puzzle that will afflict the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amber Hamur Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Amber Hamur dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and kicks two furlongs out before her rivals can organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: Amber Hamur has won over this exact trip on Good ground and, with no challenger for the lead, she can conserve energy before asking a winning question early in the straight; her recent form of 21 shows a horse in excellent heart.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is just steady enough to be caught by a horse who travels prominently close to the pace and produces the sharper finish.
scenarios.body: Hey Havana has placed twice at this trip and loves Good ground, and Vega's Virtue — a dual course-distance winner — holds a strong claims as a horse that travels smoothly and can produce a sustained challenge inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses turning in and a hold-up horse threads through as the leaders weaken in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Dacres Cross has the best recent profile among the hold-up types with sim-going form giving her any realistic claim, and Vega's Virtue's form on Good ground makes her a candidate if she gets daylight; however this scenario is compromised by the fact that the redistributed hold-up runners may not be able to race genuinely off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Scrambles
scenarios.trigger: If Amber Hamur burns out her advantage too early or checks, creating a messy finish with multiple challengers arriving together.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the uncontested nature of the pace, but in a scramble the horses who handle positional disruption best — Hey Havana and Vega's Virtue — carry the most upside through chaotic traffic.

watchPoints.text: Amber Hamur sets the entire tempo — if she is allowed to bowl along uncontested and Connor Beasley times his run from the two-furlong pole, she is the horse every other trainer and jockey is watching and planning around.

The cluster of genuine hold-up horses — Sailor's Return, Scheffler, Tago Mago and Itszaboy — are all likely to be jostling for the same ground in the rear to mid-division; watch for interference or checked momentum entering the straight as they attempt to find daylight simultaneously.

Hey Havana's prominent style is perfectly suited to sit second or third behind Amber Hamur, but if she is shuffled back by the hold-up pack during the opening furlong, she loses her tactical edge and her chance narrows significantly.

Vega's Virtue's two wins have come over exactly this course configuration and trip on Good ground — her trainer Tim Easterby is operating at 3/87 over 14 days which is modest, but the horse's own form profile is the strongest historical fit for conditions in the field.

Going is confirmed Good throughout the card at Ripon with no deterioration reported; no horse has a going concern flagged, meaning the race should be run on a true surface and form at the trip should be taken at face value.
